question: does a retrieval-layer premise-resistance rule (topic-group, newer-evidence-first demotion) move the implicit-invalidation baseline?
design: B2 rule in lite fusion: group top-k hits by lexical overlap (Jaccard >= 0.2) OR cached-vector cosine (>= 0.75), halve the older member's score within each group. Re-ran the 25-scenario STALE baseline twice: default offline profile (tfidf vectors) and bge-m3 semantic vectors.
findings: NEGATIVE: the ranking rule does not resolve implicit invalidation. With tfidf the outcome distribution is unchanged; with bge-m3 both values surface in 100% of probes yet the newer one ranks first in only 1/25.

The failure reproduces the STALE-paper diagnosis at our layer: retrieval surfaces the fresh evidence fine - the gap is inference-level state resolution (recognizing that the later observation supersedes the earlier one), which lexical or embedding similarity cannot do for paraphrased invalidation pairs.

The rule stays in the codebase behind MEMPLEX_PREMISE_RESOLUTION=1 (default off) as an inert primitive; the productive B2 direction is an orchestration-leg or maintenance-time LLM pass (premise-resistance prompting), which remains open.
honest_reading: 25 scenarios, rank-sensitive metric added for this study; both-rule runs executed with the rule enabled via env before the default was flipped to off.
